statements.text: While algorithmic tools have the potential to address bias in the hiring process, the research is clear that—without the appropriate safeguards in place—artificial intelligence and other automated technologies can further entrench discrimination against workers, including workers with disabilities.
statements.venue: Press statement on EEOC/DOJ AI hiring guidance

statements.text: The rise of AI in the workplace—as with any new technology—may displace jobs, violate workers' privacy, pose obstacles to workers' right to organize and collectively bargain, and exert a disparate impact on people of color, women, older people, and people with disabilities. [...] But our job in Congress is to do everything we can to ensure that the changing economy does not undermine the financial security, civil rights, and labor-market opportunities of American workers.
statements.venue: Remarks at roundtable on AI in the workplace (press release)

statements.text: A great day honoring “AI” @alleniverson as the @CityofNN honored him with the naming of Allen Iverson Way. He has been an immense source of pride for all of Hampton Roads. https://t.co/bWo1FOPYZI
AI is not an infallible technology, and it is not neutral. So, we must take proactive steps to ensure that AI technology does not perpetuate existing disparities and erode civil rights.
statements.venue: Opening statement, House Education & Workforce Committee hearing "Building an AI-Ready America"

statements.text: This is why Congress must take an active role in shaping how AI is integrated into our lives and develop thoughtful regulations that balance protecting students, workers, and families, and fostering economic growth. Today, we stand at another crossroads of technological advancement, and it is up to Congress to ensure that AI takes us forward, not backward.
statements.venue: Opening statement, House Education & Workforce Committee hearing "Building an AI-Ready America"

statements.text: Congress should not, however, stand idly by while the Trump Administration may be ingratiating itself with big tech CEOs and preventing states from protecting Americans against the dangers posed by AI.
statements.venue: Opening statement, House Education & Workforce Committee hearing "Building an AI-Ready America"

statements.text: The National Center for Missing and Exploited Children also reports that it is seeing a dramatic increase in generative AI technologies that are capable of creating child sexual abuse material, and a rise in other disturbing trends related to AI chatbots.
statements.venue: Opening statement, House Education & Workforce Committee hearing "Building an AI-Ready America"

statements.text: Mr. Speaker, finally, I include in the Record an article from StateScoop with a letter from Al Sharpton of the National Action Network, outlining many issues involved in identity verification done by artificial intelligence. [...] AI-driven risk models are only as fair as the data on which they are trained, and the commercial and alternative data underlying these systems systematically underrepresent and misrepresent communities of color. [...] those structural gaps are not corrected by the algorithm, they are encoded into it.
statements.context: Floor remarks by Rep. Bobby Scott of Virginia inserting into the Congressional Record a StateScoop article and a letter from Rev. Al Sharpton regarding AI-powered identity-verification vendor Socure.
